guides.definition: console.log formats its arguments and writes them to the process standard-output stream followed by a line break.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: A JavaScript expression to display.

examples.title: Display a greeting
examples.code: console.log("Hello from Hypershell");
examples.explanation: The string literal is evaluated and written to the Node.js terminal.

guides.definition: node:fs/promises readFile returns a promise for the file contents. Supplying utf8 resolves the promise with a string.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: A JavaScript string containing the file path.

examples.title: Read an isolated temporary file
examples.explanation: The promise resolves with decoded text from a file created inside an isolated temporary directory, which is then removed.

guides.definition: fs/promises writeFile replaces an existing file by default and creates it when absent. Callers should await completion and avoid overlapping writes to the same path.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: A string, Buffer, URL, or file handle identifying the file.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The string or binary content to write.

parameters.name: encoding
parameters.description: The text encoding option.

examples.title: Write and verify a temporary file
examples.explanation: The example writes 42, reads it back, and removes its isolated temporary directory.

guides.definition: fs/promises readdir resolves with entry names by default. withFileTypes returns Dirent objects, while recursive can traverse descendants on supported Node versions.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The directory path to inspect.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Encoding, withFileTypes, or recursive behavior.

examples.title: List an isolated directory
examples.explanation: The directory contains only answer.txt, then the temporary tree is removed.

guides.definition: fs/promises mkdir rejects when the target already exists unless recursive is true. Recursive creation resolves after all missing parents have been created.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The directory path to create.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Recursive and permission-mode behavior.

examples.title: Create nested temporary directories
examples.explanation: Recursive creation builds both missing levels and stat confirms the final path is a directory.

guides.definition: fs/promises stat follows symbolic links and resolves with an fs.Stats object containing type checks, sizes, and timestamps. Use lstat to inspect a link itself.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The path whose metadata is requested.

examples.title: Inspect a temporary file
examples.explanation: The Stats object identifies a file containing two UTF-8 bytes.

guides.definition: fs/promises rm can recursively remove directory trees and can ignore missing paths with force. Recursive removal should be scoped to a path the application has validated.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The validated file or directory path to remove.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Recursive, force, and retry behavior.

examples.title: Remove one temporary file
examples.explanation: The example removes only a file it created inside an isolated temporary directory.

guides.definition: fs/promises rename delegates to the operating system. Moving across file-system volumes can fail and may require an explicit copy-then-remove strategy.

parameters.name: oldPath
parameters.description: The existing source path.

parameters.name: newPath
parameters.description: The destination path.

examples.title: Rename a temporary file
examples.explanation: The created file is renamed in place and remains readable under its new path.

guides.definition: fs/promises access is useful for a direct permission check, but checking before a later operation can introduce a race. Prefer performing the operation and handling its error when possible.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The file-system path to test.

examples.title: Check a temporary file
examples.explanation: access resolves for the file created by the example, after which the temporary directory is removed.

guides.definition: path.join concatenates segments, normalizes separators and dot segments, and returns a relative or absolute path according to the supplied parts.

parameters.name: segments
parameters.description: Comma-separated string expressions passed as path segments.

examples.title: Build a nested path
examples.code:
const { join } = require("node:path");
console.log(join("reports", "2026", "summary.txt"));
examples.explanation: The segments are combined with the correct separator for the running platform.

guides.definition: path.resolve normalizes the result and uses the current working directory when the supplied segments do not establish an absolute base.

parameters.name: segments
parameters.description: Comma-separated path-segment expressions.

examples.title: Resolve a path beneath the working directory
examples.code:
const { isAbsolute, resolve } = require("node:path");
console.log(isAbsolute(resolve("reports", "summary.txt")));
examples.explanation: resolve produces an absolute path, confirmed without relying on a platform-specific spelling.

guides.definition: path.relative resolves both inputs before comparing them and returns an empty string when they identify the same location.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The starting path expression.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The destination path expression.

examples.title: Find a child path relative to its root
examples.explanation: The result identifies the nested file without embedding an operating-system-specific root.

guides.definition: path.extname includes the leading period and returns an empty string when the basename has no extension under Node's path rules.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The path string to inspect.

examples.title: Read a PDF extension
examples.code:
const { extname } = require("node:path");
console.log(extname("report.pdf"));
examples.explanation: The returned extension includes the leading period.

guides.definition: path.basename performs lexical path processing and does not access the file system. Case sensitivity of suffix removal follows normal string comparison.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The path string to inspect.

parameters.name: suffix
parameters.description: An optional exact suffix removed from the result.

examples.title: Read a filename without its extension
examples.code:
const { basename } = require("node:path");
console.log(basename("reports/summary.pdf", ".pdf"));
examples.explanation: basename selects summary.pdf and removes the exact .pdf suffix.

guides.definition: path.dirname lexically normalizes trailing separators and does not require the path to exist.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The path string to inspect.

examples.title: Read the containing directory
examples.code:
const { dirname } = require("node:path");
console.log(dirname("reports/summary.pdf"));
examples.explanation: The final filename is removed, leaving reports.

guides.definition: url.fileURLToPath handles percent encoding, drive letters, and network paths according to Node's platform rules; reading URL.pathname directly does not.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: A file URL object or string.

examples.title: Round-trip the working directory
examples.explanation: Node converts the working directory to a file URL and back using platform-correct rules.

guides.definition: url.pathToFileURL resolves relative paths and correctly escapes characters that would have special meaning in a URL.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The native path string to convert.

examples.title: Create a file URL for the working directory
examples.code:
const { pathToFileURL } = require("node:url");
console.log(pathToFileURL(process.cwd()).protocol);
examples.explanation: The resulting URL uses the file protocol on every supported platform.

guides.definition: os.platform returns values such as win32, linux, or darwin and matches process.platform. Feature detection is usually preferable when behavior can be tested directly.

parameters.name: expected
parameters.description: A platform identifier to compare.

examples.title: Compare the two platform surfaces
examples.code:
const { platform } = require("node:os");
console.log(platform() === process.platform);
examples.explanation: os.platform and process.platform expose the same platform identifier.

guides.definition: os.homedir uses operating-system account information and environment fallbacks. Applications should join child paths rather than concatenate separators manually.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: A label printed before the returned path.

examples.title: Confirm a home path is available
examples.code:
const { homedir } = require("node:os");
console.log(typeof homedir() === "string" && homedir().length > 0);
examples.explanation: The API supplies a non-empty path string for the current user.

guides.definition: os.tmpdir chooses the platform's configured temporary location. Use fs.mkdtemp to create an application-owned unique directory beneath it.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: A label printed before the path.

examples.title: Read the temporary directory
examples.code:
const { tmpdir } = require("node:os");
console.log(typeof tmpdir() === "string" && tmpdir().length > 0);
examples.explanation: The platform exposes a non-empty temporary-directory path.

guides.definition: util.parseArgs returns option values, positional arguments, and optionally token metadata. Strict mode rejects unknown options and invalid values.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: The args, options, strict, and allowPositionals settings.

examples.title: Parse one typed option
examples.explanation: The declared string option consumes the following token and exposes 42 under values.count.

guides.definition: util.inspect understands circular references, collection types, depth limits, colors, and custom inspectors. Its output is intended for diagnostics rather than stable serialization.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The value to inspect.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Depth, colors, sorting, and formatting settings.

examples.title: Inspect a nested object
examples.code:
const { inspect } = require("node:util");
console.log(inspect({ answer: 42 }, { sorted: true, colors: false }));
examples.explanation: inspect produces a readable diagnostic form without ANSI color codes.

guides.definition: util.promisify expects the final argument to be a callback whose first value is an error. APIs with unusual callback contracts can provide a custom promisified implementation.

parameters.name: callbackFunction
parameters.description: An error-first callback function to wrap.

examples.title: Promisify a small callback function
examples.explanation: The callback result becomes the fulfillment value of the returned promise.

guides.definition: crypto.createHash selects a supported digest algorithm. After digest is called, the Hash object is finalized and cannot accept more data.

parameters.name: algorithm
parameters.description: A supported digest algorithm name.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The string or binary data to hash.

parameters.name: encoding
parameters.description: The digest encoding.

examples.title: Hash a deterministic string
examples.explanation: A SHA-256 digest rendered in hexadecimal contains 64 characters.

guides.definition: crypto.randomUUID uses the platform cryptographic random-number generator and may cache random data for performance unless disabled in its options.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Controls entropy caching.

examples.title: Generate and validate a UUID shape
examples.code:
const { randomUUID } = require("node:crypto");
console.log(/^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-4[0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/.test(randomUUID()));
examples.explanation: The generated identifier matches the hexadecimal version-4 UUID structure.

guides.definition: crypto.timingSafeEqual reduces timing leakage from the comparison itself. Inputs must have equal byte lengths, and surrounding code must also avoid timing-dependent behavior.

parameters.name: left
parameters.description: The first Buffer or typed-array expression.

parameters.name: right
parameters.description: An equal-length Buffer or typed-array expression.

examples.title: Compare equal buffers
examples.code:
const { timingSafeEqual } = require("node:crypto");
console.log(timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from("secret"), Buffer.from("secret")));
examples.explanation: Equal byte sequences produce true without an early-exit byte comparison.

guides.definition: EventEmitter calls listeners in registration order when emit runs. An unhandled error event throws, so error handling should be explicit for emitters that can fail.

parameters.name: eventName
parameters.description: The string or symbol identifying the event.

parameters.name: listener
parameters.description: The function called for emitted values.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The value passed to the listener.

examples.title: Emit one named event
examples.explanation: emit synchronously invokes the registered answer listener with 42.

guides.definition: events.once resolves with an array of listener arguments and then removes its listeners. For EventEmitter instances, an error event rejects the promise while waiting for another event.

parameters.name: emitter
parameters.description: An EventEmitter or EventTarget expression.

parameters.name: eventName
parameters.description: The event to await.

examples.title: Wait for a queued event
examples.explanation: The promise is registered before the microtask emits the event, then resolves with the emitted argument.

guides.definition: events.on queues matching events until consumed and removes its listeners when iteration ends. AbortSignal can cancel a long-running iterator.

parameters.name: emitter
parameters.description: An EventEmitter expression.

parameters.name: eventName
parameters.description: The event to iterate.

examples.title: Consume one event through an async iterator
examples.explanation: The iterator yields the emitted argument array and closes when the loop breaks.

guides.definition: assert.deepStrictEqual compares prototypes, enumerable properties, collection contents, and primitive values using strict semantics appropriate for tests.

parameters.name: actual
parameters.description: The value produced by the code under test.

parameters.name: expected
parameters.description: The value the result must deeply equal.

examples.title: Compare nested values
examples.explanation: The two independently created structures contain equivalent prototypes, keys, arrays, and values.

guides.definition: assert.throws can validate an error class, regular-expression message, property object, or predicate. Use assert.rejects for promise rejections.

parameters.name: operation
parameters.description: The synchronous statement expected to throw.

parameters.name: expected
parameters.description: An error constructor, regular expression, object, or predicate.

examples.title: Require a TypeError
examples.explanation: The assertion succeeds because the callback throws the expected error class.

guides.definition: timers/promises setTimeout integrates delays with async functions and supports AbortSignal cancellation and ref control through its options.

parameters.name: delay
parameters.description: The approximate delay in milliseconds.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The fulfillment value.

examples.title: Resolve after a short delay
examples.explanation: The promise fulfills with 42 after the timer becomes eligible to run.

guides.definition: timers/promises setImmediate schedules work after I/O callbacks for the current event-loop iteration and supports AbortSignal cancellation.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The fulfillment value.

examples.title: Resolve on the next check phase
examples.explanation: The promise fulfills with the supplied value on the scheduled check phase.

guides.definition: zlib.gzipSync blocks the event loop while compressing, making it suitable for small bounded inputs or tooling. Servers should normally use asynchronous or streaming compression.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The string, Buffer, typed array, DataView, or ArrayBuffer to compress.

examples.title: Compress and restore text
examples.explanation: The gzip output round-trips through gunzip to the original text.

guides.definition: child_process.spawnSync avoids shell parsing unless shell is explicitly enabled. Callers should inspect error, status, signal, stdout, and stderr and should set bounds for untrusted workloads.

parameters.name: command
parameters.description: The executable path or name.

parameters.name: args
parameters.description: An array of literal process arguments.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Encoding, working directory, environment, timeout, and shell behavior.

examples.title: Run an isolated Node child
examples.explanation: The current Node executable runs with a literal argument array, no shell, and a timeout.

guides.definition: process.cwd reflects the process-wide working directory used to resolve relative file-system paths. process.chdir can change it for the entire process.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: A label printed before the path.

examples.title: Confirm the working directory is absolute
examples.code:
const { isAbsolute } = require("node:path");
console.log(isAbsolute(process.cwd()));
examples.explanation: Node exposes the current working directory as an absolute path.

guides.definition: process.argv is an array. The first item is the Node executable, the second is normally the script path, and later items are application arguments.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: The zero-based argument index to read.

examples.title: Inspect the executable argument
examples.code: console.log(typeof process.argv[0] === "string" && process.argv[0].length > 0);
examples.explanation: The first argument always identifies the executable used to start Node.

guides.definition: process.env values are strings when present. Assigning affects the current process and inherited child environments but does not persist system-wide settings.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: A string expression containing the environment-variable name.

examples.title: Set and remove a process-local value
examples.explanation: The value exists only in this isolated Node process and is removed before exit.

guides.definition: Buffer.from supports strings, arrays, array buffers, and other buffers. String decoding uses UTF-8 unless another supported encoding is supplied.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The string or byte source.

parameters.name: encoding
parameters.description: The string encoding used for text input.

examples.title: Encode and decode UTF-8 text
examples.code:
const { Buffer } = require("node:buffer");
console.log(Buffer.from("Hypershell", "utf8").toString("utf8"));
examples.explanation: Buffer.from encodes the string and toString decodes the same bytes back to text.

guides.definition: Buffer.alloc zero-fills by default or repeats a supplied fill value. It is safer for general use than allocUnsafe when every byte will not be overwritten immediately.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: The number of bytes to allocate.

parameters.name: fill
parameters.description: The byte, string, or Buffer repeated through the allocation.

examples.title: Allocate four initialized bytes
examples.code:
const { Buffer } = require("node:buffer");
console.log([...Buffer.alloc(4, 42)]);
examples.explanation: Every allocated byte is initialized to decimal value 42.

guides.definition: Buffer.byteLength measures encoded storage rather than JavaScript UTF-16 code units, so multibyte text can occupy more bytes than string.length reports.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The string or binary value to measure.

parameters.name: encoding
parameters.description: The encoding used to measure a string.

examples.title: Measure a multibyte character
examples.code:
const { Buffer } = require("node:buffer");
console.log(Buffer.byteLength("✓", "utf8"));
examples.explanation: The check mark occupies three bytes in UTF-8 even though it is one JavaScript character.

guides.definition: stream/promises pipeline manages backpressure, forwards failures, and destroys participating streams as needed. It is safer than manually chaining pipe calls for multi-stage work.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: A readable stream, iterable, or async iterable.

parameters.name: destination
parameters.description: A writable stream or compatible transform.

examples.title: Transform iterable text through a pipeline
examples.explanation: pipeline applies backpressure, waits for completion, and yields the transformed HYPERSHELL text.
